conversation_context.content: I want a custom Signal that tags agent answers requiring human review. How do I create it in the Weave UI?

Create it as a **custom tag signal** from the Agents view. A custom signal scores agent turns against a behavior you define and shows the result as a tag in the Agents view [S2].

**Steps in the UI** [S1]
1. Go to Forge and select your project [S1].
2. In the Weave project sidebar, click **Agents** [S1].
3. Click the **Signals** tab [S1].
4. Click **+ Create your first signal** or **New signal** [S1].
5. In the drawer, click **Custom Signal** [S1].
6. In the **Custom tags** drawer, fill in these fields [S1]:
   - **Tag name**: the label shown in the Agents view for the behavior you want to monitor.
   - **Definition**: a prompt describing the behavior to detect. Weave sends it to an LLM judge, which scores each agent turn and applies the tag when the turn matches. For your case, this is where you describe what "requires human review" means.
   - **Scorer name**: the name of the underlying scorer object.
   - **Inference model or custom runtime**: the model that scores turns. Serverless Inference is the default and uses credits from your CoreWeave Forge account.
7. Optionally, expand **Advanced** [S1]:
   - **Include tool calls** adds the turn's tool calls to the context sent to the scoring model.
   - **Only score turns matching** restricts scoring by agent, operation, tool, or model. If you leave it empty, every agent turn is scored. Multiple filters are combined with `AND`.
   - **Sample rate** sets the fraction of matching turns that get scored. Lowering it for high-traffic agents can reduce cost.
8. Click **Create signal** [S1].

After you create it, Weave scores matching turns, and the tag appears in the Agents view, including on the Signals tab [S1].

**Limits of what I found:** The docs I read give only a generic Definition example: "The user is discussing errors or issues regarding Product X." [S1] They don't give criteria for "requires human review", so you'll need to write those yourself.

The docs also say this workflow is available in CoreWeave Agent Lens [S2]. This answer covers only the Weave UI path.

output.answer:
Use two optional settings in the **Advanced** section of the **Custom tags** drawer: **Only score turns matching** for the agent, and **Sample rate** for the fraction of turns [S1].

1. Follow the same steps as before to open the **Custom tags** drawer: **Agents** > **Signals** > **New signal** > **Custom Signal** [S1].
2. Fill in the **Tag name**, **Definition**, and **Scorer name** fields [S1].
3. Expand **Advanced** [S1].
4. **Restrict to one agent:** under **Only score turns matching**, add a filter for your agent. The docs list agent, operation, tool, and model as example filter types [S1]. If you leave this empty, every agent turn is scored [S1]. If you add more filters, Weave combines them with `AND` logic, so a turn must match all of them [S1].
5. **Score about one in ten:** set **Sample rate** to the fraction of matching turns to score. For one in ten, that is one tenth of matching turns [S1]. The sample rate applies to turns that match your filters [S1].
6. Click **Create signal** [S1].

**Caveats from the docs I read:**
- The page describes **Sample rate** as a "fraction". It doesn't say whether the field expects `0.1` or `10%`, so check how the field is labeled in the drawer [S1].
- The page doesn't say how sampling is done, such as random or deterministic selection. It also doesn't say whether the result is exactly one in ten. I'd treat it as approximately one in ten and not rely on an exact count.
- The page says a lower sample rate can reduce cost for high-traffic agents [S1]. It gives no specific savings figure.
- The page doesn't give the exact filter field name for selecting an agent, so pick the agent option in the filter UI.

sources.title: Create a custom signal
sources.heading: Create a custom tag signal
sources.text:
## Create a custom tag signal

To create a custom tag signal:

1. Navigate to [Forge](https://forge.coreweave.com/wandb) and select your project.

2. In the **Weave project sidebar**, click **Agents**.

3. In the tab bar, click **Signals**.

4. On the Signals tab, click **+ Create your first signal**, or **New signal**.

5. In the drawer, click **Custom Signal**.

   ![The Custom tags drawer with Tag name, Definition, Scorer name, and Inference model fields for creating a custom signal.](https://mintcdn.com/coreweave-dbfa0e8d/3Dv_sw2eg8feUJlx/products/wandb/weave/_media/custom-signal.png?fit=max\&auto=format\&n=3Dv_sw2eg8feUJlx\&q=85\&s=b01a4b83a0ef2c7717d78efc406a1de0)

6. In the **Custom tags** drawer, configure the following fields:
   * **Tag name**: The label that appears in the Agents view for the behavior you want to monitor.
   * **Definition**: A prompt that describes the behavior you want the signal to detect. Weave sends this prompt to an LLM judge, which scores each agent turn and applies the tag when the turn matches the behavior. For example, to catch a specific product failure: "The user is discussing errors or issues regarding Product X."
   * **+ Add tag** (Optional): Click to define another tag on the same signal. For example, if you support multiple products, add a separate tag for each product so you can track frustration per product instead of only in aggregate.
   * **Scorer name**: The name for the underlying scorer object.
   * **Inference model or custom runtime**: The model used to score matching turns. [Serverless Inference](https://docs.coreweave.com/products/inference/serverless.md) is the default. CoreWeave Serverless Inference consumes credits from your CoreWeave Forge account.
   * **Include tool calls** (Optional): Expand **Advanced**, then check the box to include the turn's tool calls in the context sent to the scoring model.
   * **Only score turns matching** (Optional): Expand **Advanced**, then add one or more filters to restrict which turns the signal scores, for example by agent, operation, tool, or model. Leave empty to score every agent turn. Weave combines multiple filters with `AND` logic.
   * **Sample rate** (Optional): Expand **Advanced**, then set the fraction of matching agent turns the signal scores. For high-traffic agents, lower the sample rate to score a fraction of matching turns instead of every turn and reduce cost.

7. In the **Custom tags** drawer, click **Create signal**.

After you create the signal, Weave scores matching turns. The tag appears in the Agents view, including on the Signals tab.
sources.page_context:
# Create a custom signal

> Create a custom Weave signal to tag agent turns for a behavior you define.

> [!TIP]
>
> **This workflow is also available in CoreWeave Agent Lens.** Agent Lens is the Forge experience built for tracing, monitoring, and analyzing AI agents, with automated insights into agent failures and user intents. It uses the same trace data as Weights & Biases Weave, so the traces you already send appear there with nothing to migrate.
> [See how to do this in Agent Lens](https://docs.coreweave.com/products/agent-lens/tags/create-tag.md).

A custom signal scores agent turns against a behavior you define, then shows that result as a tag in the [Agents view](https://docs.coreweave.com/products/wandb/weave/guides/tracking/view-agent-activity.md). Weave also provides [built-in signals](https://docs.coreweave.com/products/wandb/weave/guides/tracking/view-agent-signals.md) for common cases, such as user frustration and jailbreaking. When those built-in signals don't cover what you want to monitor, create a custom signal. This page shows you how to create that custom tag signal in the Weights & Biases UI.

results.title: Monitor your agents with signals
results.heading: Create a new signal
results.snippet:
## Create a new signal

To start scoring your agent's turns, create one or more signals. Select **+ New signal** to open the **Create signals** drawer.

The drawer groups available signals into two categories:

* **Tags**: Apply a label automatically to matching spans, such as `user-frustration` or `nsfw`. Use tags to categorize spans or flag unwanted behavior. The signals UI only displays rows for spans that matched at least one tag, so a tag signal might run successfully even if you don't see any output.
* **Ratings**: Assign a score from 0 to 1 to matching spans. Use ratings to rate agent performance and measure improvements over time.

results.title: Score agent turns with a remote scorer
results.heading: How agent turn scoring works
results.snippet:
## How agent turn scoring works

An agent turn is scored in the following sequence:

1. A turn ends. When a root span (a span with no parent) ends, Weave treats it as a completed turn and emits a `weave.genai.turn_ended` event.
2. The agent scoring worker loads the project's active signals that target `weave.genai.turn_ended`, then applies each signal's filters and sample rate.
3. For each `RemoteScorer` on a matching signal, the worker builds a `schema_version: 2` request from the turn's span, including its messages, resolves the scorer's credentials, checks the endpoint URL against the allowed hosts, and sends the `POST`.
4. The worker validates the response and writes the result as feedback on the turn. Tags and ratings appear on the **Signals** tab.

Weave scores only completed turns. Individual LLM and tool spans, and whole conversations, aren't remote scoring targets. A remote scorer signal is a `Monitor` whose `op_names` is `["weave.genai.turn_ended"]`, whether you create it in the UI or with the SDK.

results.snippet:
## Signals table

The Signals tab displays a table of scored turns from your agent. Each row represents the output of one of your signal monitors. The following columns appear by default.

| Column | Description |
| - | - |
| **Type** | The part of the conversation that gets scored. Only `turn` is supported. |
| **Scorer** | The name of the signal that produced this score. |
| **Last message** | A preview of the last message in the scored turn, with the role shown below. |
| **Agent** | The agent associated with the scored turn. |
| **Scores** | The numeric rating from 0.0 to 1.0, or a tag if matched. We recommend using consistent ratings where 1 indicates good and 0 indicates bad, but your scorers can use any scale you define. |
| **Trend** | Displays an inline chart that shows how this signal trends over time. Shows either the average value (for ratings) or the count (for tags). |
| **When** | When the signal was scored. |

It uses the same trace data as Weights & Biases Weave, so the traces you already send appear there with nothing to migrate.
> [See how to do this in Agent Lens](https://docs.coreweave.com/products/agent-lens/tags/create-tag.md).

A custom signal scores agent turns against a behavior you define, then shows that result as a tag in the [Agents view](https://docs.coreweave.com/products/wandb/weave/guides/tracking/view-agent-activity.md). Weave also provides [built-in signals](https://docs.coreweave.com/products/wandb/weave/guides/tracking/view-agent-signals.md) for common cases, such as user frustration and jailbreaking. When those built-in signals don't cover what you want to monitor, create a custom signal. This page shows you how to create that custom tag signal in the Weights & Biases UI.

Use two optional settings in the **Advanced** section of the **Custom tags** drawer: **Only score turns matching** for the agent, and **Sample rate** for the fraction of turns [S1].

1. Follow the same steps as before to open the **Custom tags** drawer: **Agents** > **Signals** > **New signal** > **Custom Signal** [S1].
2. Fill in the **Tag name**, **Definition**, and **Scorer name** fields [S1].
3. Expand **Advanced** [S1].
4. **Restrict to one agent:** under **Only score turns matching**, add a filter for your agent. The docs list agent, operation, tool, and model as example filter types [S1]. If you leave this empty, every agent turn is scored [S1]. If you add more filters, Weave combines them with `AND` logic, so a turn must match all of them [S1].
5. **Score about one in ten:** set **Sample rate** to the fraction of matching turns to score. For one in ten, that is one tenth of matching turns [S1]. The sample rate applies to turns that match your filters, so the agent filter is applied first and the sample rate then reduces those turns [S1].
6. Click **Create signal** [S1].
